title: Mckenna Grace on Her ‘Hunger Games’ Press Tour Looks for ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’: Maysilee’s Style Is Her ‘Form of Defiance Against the Capitol’
description:
Mckenna Grace has been on a red carpet run for the ages during the global press tour for “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”

	Over the last
body:
Mckenna Grace has been on a red carpet run for the ages during the global press tour for “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”

	Over the last few weeks, the 20-year-old actress (and certified “Hunger Games” fangirl) has donned nearly two dozen looks that referenced the original trilogy or franchise star Jennifer Lawrence. Grace, who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner (and her twin sister, Merilee), launched the tour with an archival Monique Lhuillier gown that evoked Lawrence’s wedding dress as Katniss in “Catching Fire.” Then, for the film’s final premiere on Monday night in New York City, Grace glided onto the red carpet in a cobalt blue Pamella Roland gown — with feathered wings! — mirroring the iconic Mockingjay look that bridal gown turned into.
	

	Like Katniss, Grace’s Maysilee aims to defy the Capitol — something the actress wanted to portray in real life, too.

	“Maysilee’s form of rebellion was also her style and holding onto her personality in the face of the Capitol,” Grace told Variety’s Antonio Ferme at the New York City premiere. “I felt like I’d be doing myself a disservice not paying homage to all of the incredible performers and costume designers from the previous films.”

	Grace joined Variety for a longer chat a few days earlier, checking in on Zoom the morning after the Los Angeles fan event for “Sunrise on the Reaping,” where she recreated another of Katniss’ dresses from “Catching Fire.” With just two stops left on the press tour (Mexico and New York City), Grace is in between fittings for her final two outfits, both of which paid homage to the mockingjay that started it all. After all, her character is the original owner of the mockingjay pin.
	



	

					Joseph Zada (as Haymitch) and Mckenna Grace (as Maysilee) in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”
									Murray Close/Lionsgate
	



	Her character, Maysilee, is the hot-headed, dignified ally of Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada), who similarly wishes to take down the Capitol and stop the Hunger Games. Although District 12 is known as the poorest district, she prides herself in her fine dresses and overzealous amounts of jewelry — something she continues to prioritize after being reaped.

	“I didn’t want it to be like, ‘Oh, I’m an actor and I’m in the Hunger Games, but I still want my character to look pretty and have good, snatched makeup,’” she says. “To me, her fashion and her style isn’t a vain thing. It’s her form of defiance against the Capitol.”

	Below, Grace talks to Variety about playing Maysilee, details she included from Suzanne Collins’ novel and fangirling over franchise stars Jennifer Lawrence and Sam Claflin.
	
		You famously fought for the braid in your hair that Maysilee wore in the fan film about the 50th “Hunger Games.” Are there any other details that you fought to have included in this movie?	

	There’s a lot. I got the braid and the bangs [from the fan film]. I know this is silly and it’s not something that’s mentioned in the books, but I wanted Maysilee to have different colored eyeshadows in all the scenes that we see her in. That’s how she stood out as a twin and in District 12: all of her necklaces, dresses, jewelry and her braid. The Capitol is appointing them clothes. She can’t have her personality shine through with her fashion, which is something she really enjoys. She has this line where she’s like, “Do we all have to look like triplets?” because they put them in all the same clothes, and they’re bland. Throughout that, she’s still finding ways to stand out and be seen as a classy person. And a person, not an animal. Somebody with fashion. Somebody with personality, with dignity. So I wanted her to have that little defiance with her eyeshadow.



	

					Mckenna Grace as Maysilee in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”
									Murray Close/Lionsgate
	



	I also made sure that she wore a bunch of rings and jewelry. I made sure that her sleeves were torn off whenever we see her in the games, which is random. But in the books, it’s mentioned that whenever they see her again, she’s missing her sleeves because she ripped them off, and she has burns up her shoulders.
	

	Also, something important to me was when Haymitch and Maysilee sit down for their picnic, I got Jo [Zada] to add back in — because this was not in the original scene — where he tells Maysilee about how his mom had twin girls that didn’t make it. I told Jo and Francis [Lawrence, the film’s director] that I felt that was so important because Maysilee, for the first time, is giving Haymitch some vulnerability. And he gives that back to her. That’s so important for their relationship and such a beautiful thing for her to hear at that time. I had a lot of things that I wanted to get in there!
	
		One scene that I wish we had from the book is when Maysilee is talking about how she doesn’t want to be a twin and work behind that candy counter for the rest of her life. Have you ever thought about what she would be doing with her life if she wasn’t chosen for the games?	

	I don’t know, because I don’t think that there’s any version — I mean, of course there are ways that she’s found joy, even within the games when Haymitch brings out the juice, and they sit and have their picnic. That’s a moment of joy; that doesn’t come with worrying about all the heaviness of the world in the games. And there are moments of connection and joy throughout it, but she’s a very angry character.

	I don’t know if there is a version of Maysilee, even not being chosen by the games, where she feels truly happy in the world that she lives in or the circumstances that she was born into. She didn’t set up that system or the world that she’s in, and I don’t think that she was ever truly happy in District 12, because she was just so angry at the way that it was all designed and at the games just for existing.



	

					A scene from “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”
									Murray Close/Lionsgate
	


	
		How did you find the balance between Maysilee’s anger and her big heart in moments like when she’s braiding Ampert’s (Percy Daggs IV) token?	

	It was really fun. She is learning to be more outwardly kind and a little bit more sensitive to the others around her, and she’s learning how to be a sister and a healer and a friend more than just being angry and lashing out at everybody throughout the film. That’s kind of what her arc is. But I didn’t want that arc of her learning to be kinder to diminish her anger. I didn’t want it to be like, “Oh, this angry female character all of a sudden learns how to be a sister and a mother and a friend, and she’s not angry anymore and has found happiness in that.”
	

	While she finds happiness in being kind to the people around her and protecting them, she’s still a very angry character. It’s really important to show young women, and anyone in general, that the two can coexist. You can be very angry at the world. You can be very loud in standing up for yourself and standing up for the people around you, but you can also be kind throughout that. That’s something we lose a lot; that it has to be one or the other. But no, you can stand up; you can speak out. You don’t have to box up your emotions and the things that you believe in, or make yourself more digestible for the people around you. You can still have your personality. You can still be loud about the things that you believe in, but you can still be kind and have conversations and care about people and stick up for the people around you throughout that.
	
		As a “Hunger Games” fan, how crazy is it to see that Jennifer Lawrence and Sam Claflin are commenting on videos of you guys?	

	It is ridiculous! It’s insane. Jennifer Lawrence’s comment was so funny. And the fact that Sam Claflin is commenting on my video of me dressed up [with] Finnick’s abs painted on my shirt — that was the funniest thing. I will never not be exposed to any celebrity that I am the biggest fan of. Between him and Josh [Hutcherson] and Jen, it’s just ridiculous. It’s so surreal. We’re all such huge fans of them. Jo and I spent so many nights mulling over Josh and Jen, and I spent so long studying Sam for Finnick. It’s such an honor that they even know who I am.

	This interview has been edited and condensed for length and clarity. 

	For more from Grace, watch her episode of Variety’s Up Next, hosted by Tiana DeNicola, below:

schema.headline: Mckenna Grace on Her ‘Hunger Games’ Press Tour Looks for ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’: Maysilee’s Style Is Her ‘Form of Defiance Against the Capitol’

title: ‘Ramayana’ Star Sai Pallavi, Ravi Kishan’s ‘Spider-Man’ Anecdote, Grammy Winner Ricky Kej Light Up International Film Festival of India Opening in Goa
description: The 57th International Film Festival of India opened in Goa on Friday, with “Lagaan” director Ashutosh Gowariker setting out a “Stories Without Bor
body:
The 57th International Film Festival of India opened in Goa on Friday, with “Lagaan” director Ashutosh Gowariker setting out a “Stories Without Borders” program in his first year as festival director and Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant renewing his push for a film city in the state.

	Paweł Pawlikowski’s “Fatherland,” which shared the best director prize at Cannes this year, opened the festival. The ceremony at the Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Indoor Stadium began with the national anthem “Jana Gana Mana” and national song “Vande Mataram,” followed by a ceremonial lamp lighting with Sawant, National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) chair G. Krishna Kumar, Gowariker and several other dignitaries.
	

	Bollywood star Kartik Aaryan was in attendance, along with Sai Pallavi, who plays Sita in Nitesh Tiwari’s blockbuster “Ramayana.” Jury chairs Aanand L. Rai (“Tanu Weds Manu”), who heads the international jury, and filmmakers Madhur Bhandarkar and Himanshu Sekhar Khatua, who led the Indian Panorama feature and non-feature juries respectively, were also in the audience. The festival runs through Nov. 28.

	Three-time Grammy winner Ricky Kej set the tone with “A World of Cinema Through Music,” an orchestral performance built around a medley of film themes played with Indian instruments. It moved from “The Godfather,” “Parasite” and “Rashomon” to “The Lord of the Rings,” Satyajit Ray’s “Pather Panchali,” “Doctor Zhivago,” “The Good, the Bad and the Ugly,” “La Bamba,” Gowariker’s own “Lagaan” and “Mission: Impossible 2.” Kej returned later with a set mixing musical traditions from Italy, Mongolia, the U.S., India and the U.A.E. A peacock dance, symbolizing the festival’s Golden Peacock award,  also featured on the program.
	

	Goa has been IFFI’s permanent home since 2004, and its streets and landmarks have turned up in films such as “Dil Chahta Hai” and “Dear Zindagi.” “But our ambition goes further,” Sawant said. “We want Goa to become the place where the films are produced and completed.”

	The state’s plans include a proposed film city with facilities for pre-production, post-production, VFX and film education, which Sawant said would encourage local filmmaking, draw filmmakers from across India and open new avenues for young Goan creative professionals. He has raised the idea at earlier editions of the festival, seeking central government support for a Goa film city at the 2021 opening ceremony. Sawant also pointed to the Goa Regulation of Film Shooting Act 2021 and an online single-window permit system run by the Entertainment Society of Goa, and said the state’s film financing scheme for Goan producers is being revised to cover newer formats and digital productions. With virtual production, AI, animation and VFX changing how films are made, he said Goa wants a stake in that next phase.

	Gowariker, the Oscar-nominated director of “Lagaan,” “Swades” and “Jodhaa Akbar,” took the job in May. He told the audience that until now he had only experienced festivals as a filmmaker who flies in with a film, does a Q&A and leaves, and that his team shaped this edition by asking what stories actually do for people.

	“We live in a time when we are more connected than ever, and yet it has also become very easy to stay inside our own circle,” Gowariker said. “Borders today are not only lines on a map. They’re also habits. A story is one of the few things that can cross such a line without a passport.”

	The international program comprises 159 films from 86 countries, picked from more than 1,400 submissions, according to Gowariker, alongside 76 Indian films in 18 languages. Romanian director Alina Șerban’s “I Matter,” a Romania-Germany-Belgium production, is the mid-festival film, and Singaporean director Anthony Chen’s “We Are All Strangers” closes the event. Spain is this year’s Country of Honor and Russia the Partner Country. A showcase of 21 films from BRICS nations, a first for the festival, opens with “Ramayana” on Nov. 22.

	Fifteen films compete for five awards in the International Competition. Prize money across the festival’s jury awards totals INR1.36 crore ($147,000), including INR51 lakh ($55,000) and the Golden Peacock for best film. Rai’s jury also includes Romanian director Bogdan Mureșanu, Venezuelan sound designer María Alejandra Rojas, Thai director Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke and Argentine director Sol Berruezo Pichon-Rivière. Eighteen titles in the lineup are their countries’ Oscar submissions. The program also counts nine world premieres, two international premieres, 24 Asian premieres and 116 India premieres.
	

	The Indian Panorama section brings 25 features and 20 non-features from across the country, chosen by Bhandarkar’s and Khatua’s juries. It opens with Aditya Dhar’s Hindi-language “Dhurandhar” and Leena Yadav’s “Becoming,” a film in Ladakhi. A curated package of 15 Goan films and six award winners from the 19th Mumbai International Film Festival complete the Indian slate.

	Gowariker also spoke about the WAVES Film Bazaar, the festival’s market, where buyers, programmers and producers from Paris, Busan and London mix with filmmakers such as a young director from Guwahati in northeastern India who had ridden a train for two days to get there.

	“Sometimes a great deal of cinema begins with someone saying, ‘Come, let’s have a coffee,’ and the other person saying, ‘Sure, I have ten minutes,'” he said. “Three hours later, there’s a co-production.”

	On the heritage front, the festival marks the centenary of Polish director Andrzej Wajda and revisits the work of Prem Nazir, Suryakant Mandhare, Raj Kumar, Uttam Kumar, Shakti Samanta, composers O.P. Nayyar and Ravi across Hindi, Bengali, Marathi and Malayalam cinema. “Lagaan” celebrates its 25th anniversary at the festival.

	Two new sections, Animation and Films About Films, feature Brad Bird’s “Ray Gunn” and Barnaby Thompson’s documentary “Maverick: The Epic Adventures of David Lean.” Women directed 52 films in the international lineup and first-time filmmakers 62. Of the 21 titles across the festival’s three competitions, 10 are by women and 12 are debuts.

	Chanchal Kumar, secretary of India’s Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, said, “A border may define where a story begins, it need not define how far that story can travel.” 

	Chief guest Ravi Kishan, a Bhojpuri star and second-term Member of Parliament from Gorakhpur, looked back on a 34-year career spanning almost 700 films in Hindi, Bhojpuri, Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, Gujarati and Marathi, including Kiran Rao’s “Laapataa Ladies,” India’s Oscar entry.

	“Many years ago, I had the chance to lend my voice to Spider-Man as Tobey Maguire, and what, in Bhojpuri!” Kishan said. “Imagine there was no border and it was a blockbuster in Bihar.”

	Gowariker urged the audience to spend part of the nine days on a film they would not normally pick. “Watch at least one film in a language you do not understand, a film from a country you have not visited, and by a filmmaker whose name you have not heard,” he said. “Let the subtitles do their work. I think you will find that the border was never as wide as you thought.”

schema.headline: ‘Ramayana’ Star Sai Pallavi, Ravi Kishan’s ‘Spider-Man’ Anecdote, Grammy Winner Ricky Kej Light Up International Film Festival of India Opening in Goa

title: Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Makes $21 Million in Previews
description:
It’s time to head back to Panem with “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” this weekend.

	The latest entry in the Lionsgate series has made $
body:
It’s time to head back to Panem with “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” this weekend.

	The latest entry in the Lionsgate series has made $21 million in Thursday previews and early screenings Wednesday at the box office. It’s expected to open with more than $100 million at the box office, though the studio is more cautiously predicting an $85 million debut. However, some estimates put the sixth “Hunger Games” movie even higher at $125 million due to the franchise’s fandom and the return of some fan-favorite characters.
	

	If the opening crosses $100 million, it’ll be one of five movies this year to surpass the milestone and join “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” ($360 million), “Toy Story 5” ($159 million), “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” ($131 million) and “The Odyssey” ($123 million).

	“Sunrise on the Reaping” comes three years after the last “Hunger Games” prequel, “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.” The 2023 movie made $5.75 million in previews and opened to $44 million. It ended its run with $363 million globally, making it a success against its $100 million budget. “Sunrise on the Reaping” should open closer to the original 2010s franchise starring Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson, which will help as it carries a $150 million budget.

	The first “Hunger Games” debuted to $152 million in 2012, with 2013’s “Catching Fire” as the highest opening with $158 million and an $865 million final global tally. The final two-part “Mockingjay” movies opened with  $121 million for “Part One” and $102 million for “Part Two.”

	“Sunrise on the Reaping” tells the story of young Haymitch Abernathy, played by Woody Harrelson in the original movies and now portrayed by Joseph Zada. He becomes a tribute for the 50th Hunger Games, which brings in twice the number of kids to battle to the death. The movie also stars Mckenna Grace, Ralph Fiennes, Kiernan Culkin, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, Jesse Plemons and more.

schema.headline: Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Makes $21 Million in Previews

title: ‘MobLand’ Season 3 Starts Shooting With Tom Hardy, Helen Mirren and Pierce Brosnan
description:
Tom Hardy is officially back on set for “MobLand” Season 3, with cameras rolling this week.

	The actor, who plays fixer Harry da Souza in the Para
body:
Tom Hardy is officially back on set for “MobLand” Season 3, with cameras rolling this week.

	The actor, who plays fixer Harry da Souza in the Paramount+ crime drama, was rumored to have been booted from the show earlier this year after “creative differences” with producer David Glasser and writer Jez Butterworth amid claims he was late for set and had demanded script changes.


	But as Variety reported at the time, reports of Hardy’s axing were premature, with Guy Ritchie and Paramount+ eager to hold on to the “Mad Max: Fury Road” star, and the trio managed to patch things up soon afterwards with filming for Season 3 due to start at the end of this year. That has now come to pass.
	

	Hardy’s co-stars Helen Mirren and Pierce Brosnan also return as heads of the Harrigan crime family, playing Maeve and Conrad respectively.

	The show also stars Paddy Considine, Joanne Froggatt, Lara Pulver, Anson Boon, Mandeep Dhillon, Jasmine Jobson, Teddie Allen, Emmett J. Scanlan, Johnny Flynn, Ophelia Lovibond, Janet McTeer and Toby Jones.

	Exec producers are Glasser, Guy Ritchie, Jez Butterworth, Tom Hardy, Ivan Atkinson, Dean Baker, Ron Burkle, David Hutkin, Bob Yari and Keith Cox.

	Season 2, which Mirren called “madder and badder,” launched in Sept. with the tenth and final episode dropping today.

	Hardy attended the Season 2 premiere in London alongside Glasser, Ritchie, Mirren and Brosnan where everyone made nice for the cameras.

	Introducing the cast on stage inside the theater, Glasser called Hardy the “captain of our ship” saying he “stayed with it to the bitter end.”

schema.headline: ‘MobLand’ Season 3 Starts Shooting With Tom Hardy, Helen Mirren and Pierce Brosnan

title: Gérard Depardieu Faces New Rape and Sexual Assault Complaint Alongside Director Guillaume Nicloux and Writer Michel Houellebecq
description: French actor Gérard Depardieu is facing a new complaint alleging rape and sexual assault during the filming of Guillaume Nicloux’s “Thalasso” in 20
body:
French actor Gérard Depardieu is facing a new complaint alleging rape and sexual assault during the filming of Guillaume Nicloux’s “Thalasso” in 2018, according to an investigation published by Mediapart on Thursday.

	The complaint also names Nicloux, who directed the film, and Michel Houellebecq, one of France’s most celebrated novelists who starred alongside Depardieu.

	The alleged incident took place on Dec. 11, 2018, during a scene that was filmed by the movie’s cameras, although the screenplay did not include any sexual activity, according to Mediapart. 
	

	The complainant, an actor, alleges that she was raped by Depardieu and sexually assaulted by Houellebecq in the presence of Nicloux, whom she accuses of complicity.

	Nicloux told Mediapart that he had not witnessed “any coercion, verbal or physical opposition” during the filming of the scene. He said he was distressed to learn that the actor had experienced what she described without his realizing it, and acknowledged having apologized to her afterward.Depardieu’s lawyers, Delphine Meillet and David-Olivier Kaminski, told French radio station RTL that they were unaware of the proceedings. 

	The complaint was filed in May 2025, shortly after Depardieu stood trial for sexually assaulting two women on the set of the 2021 film “Les Volets verts.” The new allegations come just days after Depardieu withdrew his appeal against his conviction in that case, making his 18-month suspended prison sentence final.

	In a statement titled “J’entends” (“I Hear”) released Monday, the 77-year-old actor accepted responsibility for his conviction and offered “deep and sincere apologies” to those who “may have suffered as a result.”
	

	“Justice has spoken. I have been found guilty. I accept this and take responsibility for this conviction,” Depardieu wrote, according to Le Monde.

	His lawyer, Meillet, said the actor had undergone a period of reflection and wanted to avoid putting the complainants through another trial.

	“He is a man who has come a long way, who has reached a turning point, who has taken a big step after a long period of reflection and maturation,” Meillet said. “He wanted to avoid making the complainants go through another hearing, or having to go through one himself.”

	Depardieu also faces a separate rape case involving actress Charlotte Arnould, who accused him of assaulting her in 2018. An investigating judge has ordered the actor to stand trial, a decision he is contesting. The Paris appeals court is expected to rule on Nov. 26 on whether the case will proceed to trial. Depardieu has denied the allegations made by Arnould.

schema.headline: Gérard Depardieu Faces New Rape and Sexual Assault Complaint Alongside Director Guillaume Nicloux and Writer Michel Houellebecq

title: Rich Eisen’s ‘Beautiful Day’: Landing All Four Members of U2 as Guests
description: Rich Eisen came out on to the set of his long-running talk show the other day, only to find Bono from U2 doing an impression of the running-man log
body:
Rich Eisen came out on to the set of his long-running talk show the other day, only to find Bono from U2 doing an impression of the running-man logo that has long been a part of the program’s identifying marks. When Eisen went to take part, he discovered the person taking pictures of the encounter wasn’t the program’s staff photographer, but rather The Edge.

	Eisen calls it being “stuck in a moment I didn’t want to get out of.” And that’s the last U2 song joke we’ll make here.
	



	The host has long been known for his sportscasting and “The Rich Eisen Show” has long been featured as part of sports programming, but that doesn’t mean the host and the program can’t take a detour once in a while.

	“This is what our show is about. It’s a pop culture show,” Eisen says during a recent interview. “Sports is just one spoke on the pop culture wheel.” U2 holds forth with Eisen on Friday’s program.

	Eisen has over the years talked with Jon Bon Jovi, Jodie Foster, James Taylor, Will Ferrell, Kenny Chesney and Snoop Dogg, and there are reasons for him to do so. Since returning to the ESPN empire (Eisen was an ESPN regular between 1996 and 2003), Eisen’s show now streams on Disney+ and the ESPN App, among other venues.

	“We are exposed to a much larger audience of movies, television, music and sports fans,” says Eisen, adding: We put the word out 12 years ago that, yes, we are on sports talk radio, and yues, I’m known certain in my other jobs as a sportscaster, but I’m just as into movies and music and TV shows and live theater as anybody else.”
	

	How did Eisen’s team land U2? The band, which just released its first full album, Carnaval de Luz, in nine years, is scheduled to play the halftime show of Netflix’s stream of a Thanksgiving Eve game taking place between the Green Day Packers and the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. That’s not too far from the studio that houses Eisen’s show. Liz Walid, co-executive producer of the show, reached out. The band’s publicist seemed willing.

	Eisen says he didn’t spend hours trying to come up with questions that would ferret out some small detail that fans don’t already know. Instead, his focus is on trying to create “a good hang.”

	“The way I approach it is just to ask them questions that I’m curious to know the answers to,” the host says. “If I somehow unearth something that hasn’t been talked about, then so be it.” Eisen and his staff have devised a Q&A segment that plays well  on YouTube in which he asks guests to confirm or knock down stories and memes about them that are already at play in the digi-sphere. The exchanges, he says, are popular.

	The “Eisen” team hopes for more. “We take the show seriously but we don’t take ourselves seriously,” says Eisen. “We are open for business every day.”

schema.headline: Rich Eisen’s ‘Beautiful Day’: Landing All Four Members of U2 as Guests

title: Robert Pattinson’s Bond Ascent: How Pricey Screen Tests and Amazon Execs Landed a Starry 007
description:
What does an actor do in the quiet moments before the announcement that will change his life? 

	For Robert Pattinson, there were about 12 hours be
body:
What does an actor do in the quiet moments before the announcement that will change his life? 

	For Robert Pattinson, there were about 12 hours between the Sunday phone call confirming he’d landed the role of James Bond and Amazon MGM’s Monday-morning release of the first image of the actor rocking a tuxedo and pistol. He spent it, rather predictably, watching an arthouse horror film. 


	His longtime friend and collaborator Robert Eggers told Variety this week that Pattinson was screening the director’s forthcoming genre drama “Werwulf” when the Bond news broke. Nothing like a stark naked Aaron Taylor-Johnson terrorizing a quaint village to pass the time.
	

	But after months (years, really) of toiling and speculation over who would replace Daniel Craig in the film adaptations of Ian Fleming’s spy novels, Pattinson took the crown. It buttons up a delicious, messy and very public guessing game over which lucky man would land the iconic role. When Amazon MGM bought out rights to James Bond from longtime custodians the Broccoli family in 2025, intentions were set for a young star who could shoulder the franchise for a decade or two. An A-list team of producers (Amy Pascal of “Spider-Man” and David Heyman of the “Harry Potter” movies) recruited Denis Villeneuve to direct. Together, with significant influence from Amazon execs Courtenay Valenti and Mike Hopkins (and yes, Jeff Bezos), they screen-tested a laundry list of virile performers — including Callum Turner, Tom Francis, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor — earlier this year. 

	For the curious, the batch of screen tests cost Amazon MGM between $300,000 and $500,000 to pull off, ostensibly in secret (everyone found out), sources familiar with the process say. But two wildcard actors who tested at the last minute — “Superman” star Nicholas Hoult and the DCU’s reining Batman, Pattinson — tipped the scales. Villeneuve’s voice became the most trusted in the room on the matter of Bond’s casting, two insiders tell Variety. 
	

	His shorthand with Pattinson from working on “Dune: Part Three” made the choice inevitable, according to industry insiders — especially after Turner, the early favorite, came under scrutiny against more established names like Hoult and Pattinson. Lowden, the heat-seeking star of “Slow Horses,” was even the subject of a suspected sabotage campaign when paparazzi footage circulated showed the actor bungling an on-set motorcycle stunt just two weeks before the Bond casting was confirmed. 

	A sect of the internet lost its mind when Variety reported earlier this month that Harry Styles and Theo James were both in talks for the role. It’s rare, even by tentpole movie standards, that such a long list of candidates would flow so freely through public channels. The studios hate it because it makes them seem indecisive, one exec says. Talent absolutely hates it because the also-rans will have to answer for almost being James Bond on talk show couches and podcasts for the next 10 years. 

	“Whatever, it’s really fun,” one top talent rep tells Variety of the audition merry-go-round. 

	While there will be detractors, it’s inarguable that the Bond gig now enshrines Pattinson in the upper echelons of movie stardom. He was already well on his way, with even civilian social media pundits having commented on the “generational run” Pattinson has been living out onscreen in films like “Primetime,” “The Odyssey,” “The Drama,” “Die My Love” and, obviously, “The Batman.” That’s to say nothing of the deeply indie era (“Good Time,” “The Lighthouse”) that followed major franchise moments like his star-making turn in the “Twilight Saga” movies and a prominent role in “Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire.” The new job also represents a major win for Pattinson’s agent of more than 20 years, Stephanie Ritz of WME. Ritz and team have managed to populate massive IP with Pattinson’s face while still allowing the actor to take risks and brand himself a maverick for the cross-generational devotees of studios like A24. 

	Given the shocking November news that DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran had been jettisoned by the David Ellison regime, it’s doubtful Pattinson would linger long as Matt Reeves’ caped crusader — freeing him up to embody the sultry British charm and execute the bare-knuckle action audiences have come to expect from 007. Art-house horror movies may have to take a back seat.

title: Sofia Coppola Pays Tribute to Late Mother Eleanor Coppola at Chanel-Hosted Paris Screening of ‘Making Marie Antoinette’
description: Sofia Coppola paid tribute to her late mother, Eleanor Coppola, at the Paris premiere of the documentary “Making Marie Antoinette,” which she direc
body:
Sofia Coppola paid tribute to her late mother, Eleanor Coppola, at the Paris premiere of the documentary “Making Marie Antoinette,” which she directed, charting the making of her daughter’s 2006 cult film starring Kirsten Dunst.

	While she was unable to attend after coming down with the flu, Coppola sent a heartfelt note honoring her mother, who “taught (her) so much, especially how to look for and see beauty around you.”


	The letter was read by producer Lorenzo Mieli at the special screening, which was hosted by Chanel at the newly restored Le Saint-Germain-des-Prés cinema in Paris and marked the 20th anniversary of “Marie Antoinette.”
	

	Cannes Film Festival chief Thierry Frémaux was also on hand to introduce the documentary and reminisced about selecting “Marie Antoinette” for the festival in 2006. Frémaux recalled being immediately struck by how bold and distinctive Coppola’s take on the French queen was, and feeling that the film belonged in the festival’s official competition.

	The documentary, which world-premiered at Telluride and has been streaming on Mubi since Nov. 6, draws on footage shot by Eleanor Coppola during the epic production of “Marie Antoinette,” capturing her daughter’s creative process, as well as moments of doubt, intimate moments with Dunst and Schwartzman, sprawling rehearsal scenes, and shedding light on the craftsmanship behind the film’s elaborate costumes, sets and decor. “Making Marie Antoinette” also offers a glimpse of the Coppola family at work, with Sofia’s brother Roman Coppola directing second-unit footage and her father, Francis Ford Coppola, dropping by the set to offer advice.
	

	“My mom shot 80 hours of footage on the set of Marie Antoinette twenty years ago, and it was never put together the way she imagined. During lockdown we went through the footage and started to think about how it would take shape,” Coppola wrote. “On that set, my mom took great pleasure in recording all the detail that went into the making of the film – the costumes, Milena’s artistry, KK’s production design, the exquisitely elaborate food, flowers and decor.”

	“Having her on set meant there was a behind the scenes crew I didn’t feel self conscious in front of and nice to have my mom there during a challenging production. It was a surprise watching the footage for the first time with her, including her meeting my husband, Thomas, for the first time on camera,” Coppola continued.

	Eleanor Coppola, who died in April 2024 at age 87, was an acclaimed documentary filmmaker best known for “Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker’s Apocalypse,” which chronicled the notoriously troubled production of Francis Ford Coppola’s “Apocalypse Now.”

	In its review out of Telluride, Variety described “Making Marie Antoinette” as “lush, intimate and compulsively watchable,” praising Eleanor Coppola’s affectionate portrait of her daughter and the creative process behind the film. The review also highlighted a poignant moment in which Eleanor recalls a young Sofia pretending to direct on the set of her father’s “Apocalypse Now,” before growing up to direct her own period epic and carve out a place for herself in the still largely male-dominated film industry.

	“My daughter is directing it with clarity, grace, and her own hip approach to history,” Eleanor wrote in her diary, as quoted in Variety’s review.

	The screening was supported by Chanel, which has maintained a longstanding creative relationship with Sofia Coppola, a house ambassador. The French luxury brand previously designed the wedding dress worn by Cailee Spaeny in Coppola’s 2023 film “Priscilla” and has supported filmmaking documentaries including “Room 999” and Richard Linklater’s “Nouvelle Vague.”

	“Making Marie Antoinette” is produced by Sofia Coppola, Mieli, Mario Gianani, Rachel Dengiz and Youree Henley for Our Films, a Mediawan company, and American Zoetrope. The documentary is financed by Our Films, Mediawan Rights and Entourage Media.

schema.headline: Sofia Coppola Pays Tribute to Late Mother Eleanor Coppola at Chanel-Hosted Paris Screening of ‘Making Marie Antoinette’

title: ‘Bouchra’ Filmmakers Orian Barki and Meriem Bennani on Crafting the 3D-Animated, Autofiction Film: ‘Through Specificity, You Can Reach Truth’
description:
Meriem Bennani never set out to make a movie quite as personal as “Bouchra.”

	“I’m a pretty private person — hard to believe, probably, after seei
body:
Meriem Bennani never set out to make a movie quite as personal as “Bouchra.”

	“I’m a pretty private person — hard to believe, probably, after seeing this film,” Bennani joked, sitting with her co-director Orian Barki for a Variety’s Screening Series Q&A.

	Sure, the animated film was always a work of autofiction: “Bouchra” explores the journey of a 35-year-old Moroccan lesbian navigating life and love in New York City and writing the script for an autobiographical film. (Bouchra, the title character, is a jackal and all the cast are anthropomorphic animals, mirroring the duo’s first project, the 2020 web series “2 Lizards.”) The movie was also inspired by Bennani’s mother’s reaction to her coming out as queer. But the movie wasn’t supposed to be about their relationship. So how did it end up that way?
	

	Bennani and Barki had begun developing the project with their collaborators, cinematographer John Michael Boling and head of animation Jason Coombs, but something wasn’t quite clicking.

	“We had the script, but as we were editing the dialogues and starting to put the storyboards [together], we felt like there was something we were still looking for, and it’s the heart of the film,” Bennani recalled.

	So, she told Barki she needed to call her mom to get more insight into her perspective. Why did she react that way when Bennani came out? The call was purely for research, but Bennani knew it’d be prudent to record the conversation.



	

					“Bouchra”
									Courtesy of 2 Lizards Productions
	



	“I knew I would be too emotional to be there as a director. I would be there as a daughter,” she explained. “So I recorded them and then I played them for Orian. … And we knew in that moment, that was the film and that we needed to put these conversations in the film.”
	

	Those recordings became the new framework for the movie as the filmmakers lasered in on this personal narrative over a more synthesized version of a Moroccan lesbian’s experience.

	“Through specificity, you can reach truth,” Bennani said. “And when I say truth, I don’t mean realism. Just an emotional truth.”

	The experimental indie film debuted as part of Bennani’s art exhibition at Fondazione Prada in Milan (which backed the film), then was part of the official selection at TIFF in 2025. The feature has picked up a handful of prizes as it traveled the art house and film festival circuits, including the Gold Q-Hugo prize at the Chicago International Film Festival. (“Bouchra” is now streaming on Mubi.)

	“People are really into seeing a film that is original and looks different and is so handcrafted,” Barki said, reflecting on the positive response. “I was happy to see that people are just down for a new story and a new visual.”

	One of the most poignant pieces of feedback came from a friend who told Barki, “I always thought that my parents loving me means that they have to understand everything about me. And maturing, I learned that I can receive their love without them having to actually understand every detail of my existence the same way that I understand it.”

	Without necessarily intending to, Barki’s friend had zeroed in on a central theme of the meta movie.

	“The movie is about a mother-daughter relationship that has this foundation of love, [which] is what gets them to have all these conversations,” Barki explained. “And in a way, it doesn’t matter if they’ll understand everything about it, but just the willingness to have this conversation is already the acceptance and the love.”

	Watch the video above to learn more about Bennani and Barki’s artistry; how they drew inspiration from Wong Kar-wai’s “Chungking Express” and Martin Scorsese’s “After Hours”; and what Bennani’s mother made of the finished film.



	

					Meriem Bennani and Orian Barki speak onstage with Variety’s Angelique Jackson at the PMC Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles.
									JC Olivera

schema.headline: ‘Bouchra’ Filmmakers Orian Barki and Meriem Bennani on Crafting the 3D-Animated, Autofiction Film: ‘Through Specificity, You Can Reach Truth’

title: CNN Films Acquires Documentary ‘Bernie Taupin: Life, Music, Elton & Me’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: CNN Films has acquired “Bernie Taupin: Life, Music, Elton & Me,” a documentary about the lyricist behind such durable pop hits as “Your Song,” “Tin
body:
CNN Films has acquired “Bernie Taupin: Life, Music, Elton & Me,” a documentary about the lyricist behind such durable pop hits as “Your Song,” “Tiny Dancer” and Rocket Man,” and a longtime collaborator with Elton John.  The film will debut on CNN Friday, January 1 at 8 p.m., continuing a tradition at the Skydance network of kicking off a new year with an intimate portrait of an intriguing figure.

	“I’ve spent much of my life telling stories, so it’s a curious experience to find yourself the subject of one,” says Taupin, in a statement. “There’s quite a distance between the life I imagined as a kid in Lincolnshire and the one I’ve been fortunate enough to live.”
	

	Taupin has largely remained out of the spotlight, while John sang his words. The new film features intimate conversations with Taupin, including a rare sit-down with John, who reminisces about their shared history. Director Matthew Miele uses the film to explore Taupin’s passions and artistic influences.

	“I wanted to explore the imagination behind those words and the singular mind that has helped shape the soundtrack of our lives,” Miele says in a statement. “Bernie afforded me rare access to his creative world, revealing an unconventional approach to songwriting in which he paints abstract portraits with words, conjuring images, characters, and emotions that often defy literal interpretation.”CNN Films has previously featured films that explored the lives of Linda Ronstadt and Glen Campbell, among others.  “Bernie Taupin: Life, Music, Elton & Me” is directed and executive produced by Matthew Miele. Producers are Derik Murray for Network Entertainment and Stephen McCormack for Reflektor Media. The film is executive produced by Gary Oldman, Charlie Hendon, Greg Zeschuk, Tim Gamble, Brian Gersh, Kent Wingerak, Greg Zeschuk, and Jody Gerson and David Blackman for Polygram Entertainment. CNN Films has acquired television and SVOD rights for the US and Canada.

title: Reinaldo Dennes Execution Takes Over an Hour as Prisoner Complains of Pain: 'I Don't Think This Is Normal'
description:
Texas Execution
                          Takes Over an Hour, Prisoner Complains of Pain
body:
Texas Execution
                          Takes Over an Hour, Prisoner Complains of Pain
                          ... 'Don't Let Me Suffer!'
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 20, 2026
                            5:29 AM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 20, 2026
                                6:53 AM PST
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
              The execution of Reinaldo Dennes took over an hour yesterday as he complained of pain during the procedure.
      
    
              Dennes was ultimately put to death in Texas Thursday ... but not before prison staff struggled to find a vein in order to hook up an IV line for the lethal pentobarbital ... AP News reported.
      
    
              After he shared a brief statement, he told the warden to "go!"
      

              Dennes then shouted ... "The pain! Go! Go!"
      
    
              Asking "the father" to "take this pain," he added ... "My right leg is killing me! ... I don't think this is normal. Take me, father. Don't let me suffer like this. C'mon."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
              Dennes then began snoring loudly before breathing more quietly. After 64 minutes elapsed since the start of the procedure, he was eventually declared dead.
      
    
              Despite the lengthy execution, prison officials claimed that while they struggled to find a vein, they said they followed procedures to the T, and nothing was abnormal.
      
    
              And as for the claims of pain? Texas Department of Criminal Justice spokesperson Amanda Hernandez said ... "This isn’t the first time we had to insert IVs into other locations. It’s also not the first time we’ve had an inmate make allegations of pain immediately."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              The hour-long execution of Dennes -- who had been convicted of the 1996 murder of Janos Szucs -- comes almost two months after the botched procedure meant to put Christa Pike to death in Tennessee.

title: 'Euphoria' Hunter Schafer Seeking Monogamy After Exploring 'Queer' Open Relationships
description:
'Euphoria' Hunter Schafer
                          I Want To Be Monogamous ...
body:
'Euphoria' Hunter Schafer
                          I Want To Be Monogamous ...
                          After 'Queer' Open Relationships
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 20, 2026
                            6:20 AM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Hunter Schafer says she's ready for monogamy in her next relationship after making the rounds in the "queer" community and exploring open relationships.
      
    
              The "Euphoria" star sat down for a wide-ranging interview Thursday with Cosmopolitan Editor-in-Chief Willa Bennett for Cosmo's "Blind Date" series, and Hunter discussed her sexual preferences, as well as her stance on monogamy.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Bennett kicked things off by asking how Hunter was feeling about monogamy these days, and Hunter didn't hold back, responding, "I've done my rounds in like the queer community, moving through queerness, operating in different forms of queerness, done the open thing, done the poly thing, and I think I like monogamy."
      

              Hunter added ... "I think I do [like monogamy]. I think it's nice and sweet, and it's less complicated." She went on to say that not being monogamous "comes with more work a lot of the time" from a scheduling standpoint.
      
    
              Bennett then chimed in to say that as a queer person herself, she would prefer to be open-minded regarding a non-monogamous relationship, but she believes it would "be really hard" for her.
      
    
              Hunter replied that she feels the same way, pointing out that there are some good books on the "concept" of monogamy.

title: Skai Jackson's Baby Daddy Sentenced to 5 Years, 6 Months in Prison
description:
Skai Jackson's Baby Daddy
                          Deondre Burgin Sentenced to 5 Years, 6 Months
body:
Skai Jackson's Baby Daddy
                          Deondre Burgin Sentenced to 5 Years, 6 Months in Prison
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 20, 2026
                            7:37 AM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Skai Jackson's baby daddy Deondre Burgin has been sentenced to five and a half years behind bars in his federal case involving a gun, drugs, and a stolen car ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
              According to court docs, obtained by TMZ, Burgin pled guilty to possession with intent to distribute marijuana, possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, and receipt of a stolen motor vehicle.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
              In addition to his 66-month sentence, Burgin is set to be transferred to the Southern District of Ohio to face separate federal charges.
      

              Per the court docs, after Burgin is released, he’ll be put on 5 years of supervised release with drug testing requirements and must participate in a substance abuse and/or mental health treatment program.
      
    
              He was also ordered to pay a $300 special assessment and $20,000 in restitution, along with forfeiting a Glock handgun and all of its ammo.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              We reported earlier ... authorities say two masked men attacked another man by his Mercedes in Cincinnati, Ohio, in June 2025 ... with one of them pistol-whipping him, which resulted in a warrant being issued for Burgin's arrest.
      
    
              The feds investigated and say the phone dropped at the carjacking scene identified Burgin as its user and claim there were messages arranging for gun and drug sales and hundreds of photos of Burgin posing with firearms and bags of marijuana -- including a pic of him wearing the same red hat agents had previously observed and photographed next to marijuana during a previous raid of his bedroom in Kentucky.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              In July of that year, the docs say Burgin copped to owning the Glock and marijuana seized from his bedroom during the raid -- and admitted he bought a stolen Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat knowing it was likely a hot car.
